text: Heritage Toronto is working with the Horse Racing Hall of Fame, a charity, and local residents to commemorate the location of the Carleton Race Course. This plaque will inform residents and visitors on Toronto's early horse-racing, sports, and entertainment histories. The Carleton Race Course was built in the late 1850’s by William Conroy Keele on his farm land in the West Toronto Junction. The course was bounded on the west by what is now High Park Avenue, on the south by Glenlake Avenue, on the east by Pacific Avenue and the north by Annette Street. The club house was most likely positioned at a central point on the west side near High Park Avenues and Humberside Avenue. The race course land became the headquarters of the Toronto Turf Club.
